ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a circle with K as the center. Points L and J are on the same straight line, and this straight line passes through the center K and intersects the circle; the segment from K to the circle is labeled 10, indicating that the radius is 10. The left endpoint of chord MN is M, and the lower-right endpoint is N. Line LJ intersects chord MN at point P, and a right angle is marked at P in the figure, indicating that LJ is perpendicular to MN. Reasoning: It is known that MN=16. Because the radius or diameter through the center of the circle is perpendicular to chord MN, it bisects chord MN, so PN=16/2=8. Connect K to N; then KN is a radius, so KN=10. In right triangle KPN, KP=sqrt(KN^2-PN^2)=sqrt(10^2-8^2)=sqrt(36)=6. Also because KL is also a radius, KL=10. P is located between K and L, so LP=KL-KP=10-6=4. In right triangle LPN, LN=sqrt(LP^2+PN^2)=sqrt(4^2+8^2)=sqrt(80)=8.944..., which rounded to the hundredth is 8.94. The given degree measure of arc MN, 98, does not need to be used in this solution.

method.method_draft: Read the image as a circle centered at K, with LJ passing through K and meeting chord MN at P at a right angle. The segment from K to the circle is labeled 10, so the radius is 10. From the text, use MN=16. Apply the theorem that a radius/diameter perpendicular to a chord bisects the chord, so PN=8. In right triangle KPN, compute KP=sqrt(10^2-8^2)=6. Since KL is also a radius, KL=10, so LP=KL-KP=4. Then use right triangle LPN: LN=sqrt(LP^2+PN^2)=sqrt(4^2+8^2)=sqrt(80), rounded to 8.94. The given arc measure can be treated as unused or extraneous because the radius/chord data already determine LN.
